verdicts.reading: Genetic modification of embryos before birth is used in health care around 2020. Mitochondrial replacement (germline change to the embryo's mitochondrial DNA), debated in the UK in 2012 as embryo genetic modification, falls within the label. Test: real clinical use by 2022.
verdicts.reason: CRISPR editing of embryos (He Jiankui, 2018) was criminalised and abandoned. But Newcastle has held a clinical licence for mitochondrial donation by pronuclear transfer since 2017, inside the NHS pathway though framed as a research study, and eight babies were reported in 2025. Licensed, tiny-scale use within the window = D37 partial. A misses this path; a strict nuclear-editing reading would give miss, which is why this call is less certain.

evidence.title: Eight babies born after Mitochondrial donation (Newcastle University)
evidence.shows: First clinical licence for pronuclear transfer 2017; eight babies born; run within the NHS Mitochondrial Reproductive Care Pathway as a research study

evidence.title: Chinese Researcher Who Created Gene-Edited Babies Sentenced To 3 Years In Prison
evidence.shows: CRISPR embryo editing path prosecuted and abandoned

verdicts.reading: Visual-to-auditory sensory substitution devices are used in health care (vision rehabilitation) around 2020. Test: any real use in care or rehabilitation by 2025.
verdicts.reason: The vOICe has been free since the 1990s, and a handful of blind individuals use it daily, but reviews describe these devices as used mainly in research, not in practical rehabilitation. No rehab service or care pathway adopted them by 2025. Scattered self-use by a few individuals is not use in health care. A's own evidence shows availability, not use in care.

evidence.title: Sensory substitution: Closing the gap between basic research and widespread practical visual rehabilitation
evidence.shows: SSDs mainly used in research, not adopted for practical visual rehabilitation

evidence.title: A self-training program for sensory substitution devices (PLoS One)
evidence.shows: Only a few SSDs used outside the lab; none adopted by a wide blind community

evidence.title: The vOICe: Seeing with Sound
evidence.shows: Free app available; no adoption or clinical-use figures
